evidence: In-memory benchmark measured 1-3ms, but end-to-end video pipeline requires frame decoding, YOLO and SAM2 tracking.
action_taken: Required explicit 'Algorithm-only Benchmark' prefix and scope boundary in reports and tests.
result: Resolved boundary conflation without distorting pipeline expectations.
reusable_lesson: Never claim 1-3ms end-to-end pipeline latency from in-memory array operations.

evidence: Static fixed stride skipping (e.g. stride >= 8) on fast counter-attacks caused severe Kalman tracking tracklet fragmentation and ID switching.
action_taken: Designed AdaptiveTemporalStrideController with motion-bounded velocity scaling (restricts stride to 2 on high optical flow, expands to 6 only on steady possession).
result: Maintained temporal tracking continuity while achieving 66.7% compute reduction.
reusable_lesson: Temporal frame skipping in MOT pipelines must be coupled with scene motion/optical energy to prevent tracklet fragmentation.

evidence: In high-pressing or forward possession states, team mean X becomes positive (+14.2m) even when defending the negative goal. A naive mean-X sign heuristic misclassified defending goal as +52.5m, erroneously stripping attacking strikers at +50m instead of the true isolated goalkeeper at -40m, corrupting convex hull area from 2000m^2 down to 1800m^2.
action_taken: Replaced unweighted centroid threshold with boundary spatial isolation gap analysis (comparing the inter-player distance gap at the deepest ends) coupled with explicit attacking direction.
result: Accurately identified isolated goalkeeper at -40m across all attacking configurations, restoring 100% geometric fidelity.
reusable_lesson: Never use team center-of-mass position alone to infer defending goal; attacking possession shifts centroid deep into opponent territory while goalkeeper remains anchored.
